subject: ordering of factor levels in colext

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: ordering of factor levels in colext
parts:
Dear all,

this is really an R question, I admit, but perhaps somebody wants to help anyway. I've been running some simulations with colext fitting dynamic occupancy models to 10-year data. I was shocked to find that the estimates of p did not seem to bear any resemblance with the input values (but those for psi, gamma and eps did !).

I just found out that this seems to be due to the way in which R orders factor levels; see e.g. this table of estimates:
       Estimate SE  z P(>|z|)
year1    -3.498 NA NA      NA
year10   -1.060 NA NA      NA
year11   -7.796 NA NA      NA
year12   -0.801 NA NA      NA
year13   -1.703 NA NA      NA
year14   -1.304 NA NA      NA
year15   -3.650 NA NA      NA
year16   -1.183 NA NA      NA
year17   -2.768 NA NA      NA
year18   -0.996 NA NA      NA
year19   -1.410 NA NA      NA
year2    -1.714 NA NA      NA
year3    -0.810 NA NA      NA
year4    -1.437 NA NA      NA
year5    -0.782 NA NA      NA
year6    -1.220 NA NA      NA
year7    -1.076 NA NA      NA
year8    -1.714 NA NA      NA
year9    -1.897 NA NA      NA

I tried several things but could not find the solution. For instance, defining year as containing a factor with ordered levels did not help:


year <- matrix(factor(1:K, ordered = TRUE), nrow(yy), data$K, byrow=TRUE)


Can anybody help ?

Thanks a lot and kind regards  --  Marc

messages.author: 3d5c753ab9984eeb
messages.subject: RE: ordering of factor levels in colext
parts:
Marc

You could try specifying the factor levels in the order you want.

Compare:

factor(paste('year',1:19,sep=''), levels=paste('year',1:19,sep=''))

factor(paste('year',1:19,sep=''))

Murray

messages.author: caaac2dc0aae28b8
messages.subject: Re: ordering of factor levels in colext
parts:
Marc;
Here is a script which illustrates how I change factor levels - hope this helps.
Eric Stolen
 
#create a data base of annual mean high temperature (data made up)
MONTH <- factor(c("JAN","FEB","MAR","APR","MAY","JUN","JUL","AUG","SEP","OCT","NOV","DEC"))
TEMP <- c(12,10,14,16,16,25,28,29,25,22,18,14)
Ann.Temp <- data.frame(MONTH,TEMP)
#plot a graph
with(Ann.Temp,plot(MONTH,TEMP))   #opps out of order
#examine variable
str(Ann.Temp$MONTH)
Ann.Temp$MONTH[1]
as.numeric(Ann.Temp$MONTH[1])
#re-order factor levels
Ann.Temp$MONTH2 <- factor(Ann.Temp$MONTH, levels=c( "JAN","FEB","MAR","APR","MAY","JUN","JUL","AUG","SEP","OCT","NOV","DEC"))
#examine variable
str(Ann.Temp$MONTH2)
Ann.Temp$MONTH2[1]
as.numeric(Ann.Temp$MONTH2[1])
#plot a graph
with(Ann.Temp,plot(MONTH2,TEMP))   #opps out of order
##THE WROnG WAY TO DO IT
Ann.Temp$MONTH3 <- factor(Ann.Temp$MONTH, labels=c( "JAN","FEB","MAR","APR","MAY","JUN","JUL","AUG","SEP","OCT","NOV","DEC"))
#look at results (seems OK?)
str(Ann.Temp$MONTH3)
Ann.Temp$MONTH3[1]
as.numeric(Ann.Temp$MONTH3[1])
#But the values have been changed!
cbind(Ann.Temp$MONTH,Ann.Temp$MONTH2,Ann.Temp$MONTH3)   #this is subtle - R stores factors as numeric variables
Ann.Temp[,c("MONTH","MONTH2","MONTH3")]                 #here we can see that the data values have been preserved in MONTH2
